title: What Oliver said of New Orleans: Keppard and Bolden
summary: Oliver talked mainly about Freddie Keppard and admired Buddy Bolden's style.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Did Oliver talk much about the early days in New Orleans to the younger musicians, like yourself, or even, say, Louis Metcalf or Elkins? Did he talk much about that period?
Well, he talked mostly about a trumpet player from New Orleans whose name was Freddie...Freddie Keppard.

Yeah. A trumpet player. He used to talk about him all the time. Otherwise, he'd... He liked Freddie Keppard's playing very much, more than anybody in New Orleans. He didn't speak too much about Bunk Johnson.
Did he talk about Buddy Bolden?
Yes. He liked Buddy Bolden a whole lot. He liked his style, his playing.
Did he ever say that anyone played like Buddy Bolden?
No. It's kind of hard to find guys that got the sound or the tonation like Buddy Bolden. In fact, there was a song come out (well, I guess Buddy Bolden must have
wrote it), a song called "I Think I Heard Buddy Bolden Sing" -- you know, it's nothing but the Blues.
I think that came a little bit later.
